correctness.rationale: Cut-vertex separation forces each petal to have a selected nonhub vertex; removing the shared hub from any geodetic set preserves geodeticity because a hub-to-petal geodesic extends to a selected vertex in another petal. For S avoiding h, global covering is equivalent to geodetic covering of each cycle by S_i union {h}. Cyclic gaps between marked vertices must all be <=floor(n/2). Deleting a selected nonhub merges adjacent gaps, and three or more individually essential marks would give two disjoint gap pairs each longer than floor(n/2), impossible. The only essential singleton is an even antipode; allowed two-vertex configurations are exactly cyclic triple gaps meeting the bound without an antipode. Deficit-triple counting gives b(n) pairs, and independent petals multiply; real roots follow by linear factors. Direct independent graph shortest-path brute force matched exact minimal subsets and cardinality distributions on 9 bouquets and 2775 nonempty candidate subsets. Note the cut-vertex exclusion and minimum-set block reduction are PRIOR RESULTS of Ekim–Erey, not rediscovered.

value.rationale: Cycle bouquets are a natural unrestricted cactus block family; the family of all inclusion-minimal geodetic sets is a different invariant from a minimum optimum. An exact factorized enumerator gives every cardinality and count, real-rootedness/log-concavity and an unbounded upper-minus-lower geodetic gap. This self-contained global classification is mathematically useful even without a full arbitrary-cactus census.

final_claim: For t>=2 cycles glued only at common hub h, minimal geodetic sets avoid h and independently select per odd petal one of b(n)=C(ceil(n/2),2) nonhub pairs, or per even petal one antipode or b(n) nonhub pairs. Hence polynomial product_i (b(n_i) z^2 +1_{n_i even} z), min size t+number odd, max size 2t, interval spectrum and real nonpositive roots.
